question.worked_solution:
First, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +5 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4)-4+5 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2} & =-1 \\ \lambda +2 & =\pm \text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-2\pm \text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-2x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(\frac{\pi }{2})={e}^{-\pi }$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}Q{e}^{-\pi } & ={e}^{-\pi } \\ Q & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=6{e}^{-\pi },$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-2{e}^{-2x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+{e}^{-2x}(-P\operatorname{sin}⁡x+Q\operatorname{cos}⁡x).
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=6{e}^{-\pi }$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2Q{e}^{-\pi }-P{e}^{-\pi } & =6{e}^{-\pi } \\ -2Q-P & =6 \\ -2-P & =6 \\ P & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $P=-8$ and $Q=1.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-2x}(-8\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$
